stem:
A 12-day-old boy was admitted in shock, with typical male genitalia. Admission samples showed low sodium, high potassium, low glucose and a metabolic acidosis. Salt-wasting 21-hydroxylase deficiency is now confirmed. Parenteral hydrocortisone and 0.9% sodium chloride have restored perfusion, and the potassium is falling without ECG changes of hyperkalaemia. On day 2 he is alert and taking all his feeds. His parents ask whether a longer-acting steroid would be easier.

The paediatric registrar is discussing ongoing hormone replacement with endocrinology. Which plan is appropriate?

options.label: A
options.text: Give night-time prednisolone alone, with no mineralocorticoid
options.explanation: Prednisolone may be used at night as a longer glucocorticoid. It does not replace fludrocortisone when salt-wasting is the problem.

options.label: B
options.text: Switch to once-daily dexamethasone and add no fludrocortisone
options.explanation: Dexamethasone lasts longer but is the glucocorticoid most likely to interfere with growth. Switching to it also leaves salt-wasting without a mineralocorticoid.

options.label: C
options.text: Continue hydrocortisone and add oral fludrocortisone now
options.explanation: This is primary adrenal insufficiency. Hydrocortisone continues to replace cortisol, and oral fludrocortisone starts once feeds are tolerated to replace aldosterone.

options.label: D
options.text: Start oral fludrocortisone and stop the hydrocortisone replacement
options.explanation: Fludrocortisone replaces aldosterone only. 21-hydroxylase deficiency also stops cortisol production, so hydrocortisone has to continue.

options.label: E
options.text: Continue stress-dose hydrocortisone alone, with no fludrocortisone
options.explanation: Stress-dose hydrocortisone covers mineralocorticoid activity only during that dosing period. Ongoing salt-wasting still needs fludrocortisone after the child is feeding.

context:
Confirmed salt-wasting 21-hydroxylase deficiency requires replacement of both cortisol and aldosterone.

Stress-dose hydrocortisone provides mineralocorticoid activity during the acute phase. Discuss with endocrinology and add oral fludrocortisone once feeds are tolerated and continue glucocorticoid replacement.

Hydrocortisone is preferred for growing children; longer-acting glucocorticoids have greater potential to impair growth.
